name: ESLint Config Generator for UI Projects
description: A comprehensive ESLint configuration generator for UI projects supporting React, Vue, Angular, and Svelte. Includes accessibility linting, TypeScript support, Prettier integration, and best practices for modern web development.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Generate an ESLint configuration tailored to the project's framework and requirements. Detect the installed ESLint version and select the config format it supports - prefer flat config for all new work. Legacy config (.eslintrc.*) is only viable when the installed ESLint still honors it: ESLint v9.x stopped auto-searching for eslintrc but still allowed the ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false escape hatch; ESLint v10.0.0 (released 2026-02-06) removed both the env var and eslintrc/.eslintignore support entirely, making flat config mandatory on v10+. Do NOT hardcode ESLint version numbers in the decision logic; when uncertain which formats the installed version supports, consult the ESLint docs for that specific major version (URLs follow https://eslint.org/docs/v{N}/use/configure/), not /docs/latest/. CRITICAL for flat config: the module system of eslint.config.js is NOT always ESM - it follows the host project's package.json 'type' field ('module' -> ESM, otherwise CommonJS). Use eslint.config.mjs to force ESM, eslint.config.cjs to force CommonJS.
keyFeatures: Framework-specific ESLint configurations (React, Vue, Angular, Svelte)
Best practices and code quality rules
Version-aware config format selection (flat config default, legacy fallback)
Auto-detection of project framework and TypeScript usage
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the installed ESLint version by reading package.json or running 'npx eslint --version'

2. Select the config format the installed version supports. Default to flat config. The ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false escape hatch (for keeping eslintrc) is ONLY honored by ESLint v9.x - v10.0.0 removed both the env var and eslintrc support entirely. So: on v9.x you may fall back to legacy if the project intentionally opts in; on v10+ flat config is mandatory. When uncertain, consult the ESLint docs for that major version at https://eslint.org/docs/v{N}/use/configure/ (do NOT use /docs/latest/ for older versions).
3. Detect the project's framework by examining package.json dependencies (react, vue, @angular/core, svelte)
4. Detect TypeScript usage by checking for typescript dependency and tsconfig.json
5. Detect Prettier by checking for prettier dependency or .prettierrc file

6. CRITICAL when emitting flat config: decide the module system. Read package.json 'type'. If 'type' === 'module', emit ESM (import ...; export default [...]) in eslint.config.js. Otherwise emit CommonJS (const ... = require(...); module.exports = [...]) in eslint.config.js. Alternatively emit eslint.config.mjs (always ESM) or eslint.config.cjs (always CommonJS) to bypass package.json entirely.
7. Generate the base ESLint configuration using the selected format and module system, with appropriate parser and plugins
9. Add TypeScript-specific rules if TypeScript is detected
10. Add accessibility plugins (jsx-a11y for React, vuejs-accessibility for Vue)
11. Configure Prettier integration if Prettier is detected (last in the config chain)
13. Handle ignore patterns using the approach for the selected format (ignores array for flat config, .eslintignore file for legacy)
14. Add npm scripts to package.json for linting (lint, lint:fix)
15. Provide installation instructions for required dependencies
16. Generate example usage and configuration documentation

toolingSpec.goal: Generate production-ready ESLint configuration files tailored to the project's framework and TypeScript usage. The config format is chosen based on what the installed ESLint version supports, not on a hardcoded version rule. Default to flat config; fall back to legacy only when the installed ESLint version requires it.

frameworkDetection.description: Detect the project's JavaScript framework to apply appropriate ESLint plugins and rules
methods: Examine package.json dependencies for framework indicators
Check for framework-specific config files (tsconfig.json, vite.config.js, etc.)
Look for framework imports in main entry files

typescriptDetection.description: Detect TypeScript usage to add appropriate parser and rules
indicators: tsconfig.json file exists in project root

prettierDetection.description: Detect Prettier to avoid ESLint formatting conflicts
prettierDetection.configurationNote: Place the Prettier config LAST in the config chain (last extends entry for legacy, last exported object for flat) so it disables conflicting ESLint formatting rules

commonRules.description: Best practice rules applicable to all JavaScript/TypeScript projects

importOrderRules.description: Enforce consistent import organization across the project

accessibilityRules.description: Accessibility linting rules for framework-specific components

typescriptRules.description: TypeScript-specific rules when TypeScript is detected

workflow: 1. Detect installed ESLint version (npx eslint --version or check package.json)
2. Choose config format the installed version supports - default to flat config, fall back to legacy only when required
3. Detect project framework (React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, or vanilla)
4. Detect TypeScript usage (check for typescript in package.json or tsconfig.json)
5. Detect Prettier (check for prettier in package.json or .prettierrc)
6. Generate the config file in the selected format (eslint.config.js for flat, .eslintrc.js for legacy)
8. Add TypeScript parser and rules if detected
9. Add accessibility linting plugins (jsx-a11y for React, vuejs-accessibility for Vue)
10. Add Prettier integration if detected (place last in the config chain)
12. Configure ignore patterns (ignores array in flat config, separate .eslintignore for legacy)
13. Install all required dependencies (provide npm/yarn/pnpm commands)
14. Add npm scripts to package.json (lint, lint:fix)
15. Test configuration by running 'npm run lint'

moduleSystem.eslint.config.js: Follows package.json 'type' field: ESM when 'type' === 'module', CommonJS otherwise. Do NOT assume ESM.

flatConfig.status: Current default - use for all new projects and when the installed ESLint supports it
features: Integrated ignore patterns via ignores array
flatConfig.note: This is the forward-compatible format. Prefer it unless the project pins an older ESLint release that does not support it. When emitting eslint.config.js, the agent MUST inspect package.json 'type' to choose ESM vs CommonJS syntax.

legacyConfig.moduleFormat: CommonJS for .js / .cjs (module.exports = {...}); JSON or YAML for the others
legacyConfig.status: Deprecated - viable only when the installed ESLint still honors it
features: Traditional extends array with string identifiers

versionSupport.v9.x: No longer auto-searched; still loadable via ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false as a migration bridge
versionSupport.v10AndLater: NOT supported. Both eslintrc auto-search and the ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG env var were removed in v10.0.0 (2026-02-06). Flat config is mandatory.

legacyConfig.note: Before recommending legacy config or the escape hatch, check the installed ESLint major version. On v10+ neither works.

securityConsiderations: ESLint runs code from node_modules during linting - ensure plugins are from trusted sources
Review ignore patterns to avoid accidentally linting sensitive files (e.g., .env files)
Use --max-warnings flag in CI to enforce zero warnings for production code
Keep ESLint and plugins updated to get security fixes
Avoid disabling security-related rules (e.g., no-eval, no-implied-eval)
Review custom rules carefully before adding to configuration
Do not commit .eslintcache file to version control (contains file system paths)

versionDetection.principle: Detect the installed ESLint version and select the config format it supports. Do NOT hardcode version numbers in the agent's decision logic - they change over time. Treat the installed version as input. When uncertain which formats it supports, consult the ESLint docs for that specific major version, NOT /docs/latest/.
detectionMethods: Read the eslint entry in package.json devDependencies (e.g., "eslint": "^9.0.0")
Run 'npx eslint --version' to get the installed version string
If ESLint is not installed yet, install the latest version and use flat config

docsLookup.rule: When checking what an installed ESLint version supports, use versioned docs - not /docs/latest/. The latest docs describe the latest release and may not match an older installed version.
docsLookup.fallback: If the URL pattern returns 404 for the installed major, fall back to https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/ but verify the claims still apply

formatSelection.fallback: legacy config (.eslintrc.*) - only when the installed ESLint version still honors it. ESLint v9.x supports it via ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false; v10+ removed both eslintrc and the escape hatch, so flat config is the only option on v10+.
formatSelection.uncertainty: When in doubt about the installed version's support, consult the versioned docs for that major (see docsLookup) and prefer flat config

moduleSystemRules.critical: eslint.config.js is NOT always ES Module. Its module system follows the host project's package.json 'type' field.

eslint.config.js.whenPackageTypeIsModule: ES Module: 'import x from y; export default [...]'

moduleSystemRules.eslint.config.mjs: Always ES Module, regardless of package.json
moduleSystemRules.agentRule: Before emitting eslint.config.js, read package.json 'type'. When in doubt or when the project lacks a 'type' field and should stay CommonJS, emit eslint.config.cjs (or rewrite as CommonJS) to avoid 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' errors.

flatConfig.ignorePatterns: Integrated into the flat config file via an ignores array
notes: Plugin references are explicit imports/requires rather than string identifiers

legacyConfig.moduleFormat: CommonJS for .js / .cjs (module.exports = {...}); JSON or YAML for the others
legacyConfig.ignorePatterns: Separate .eslintignore file required (also removed in v10+)
notes: ESLint v8 and earlier: fully supported and auto-searched
ESLint v9.x: not auto-searched but still loadable via ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false
ESLint v10.0.0 (2026-02-06) and later: NOT supported - both eslintrc auto-search and the ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG env var were removed
Only recommend this format after confirming the installed ESLint is in a version range that still honors it

errorMessages.missingFlatConfig: ESLint couldn't find an eslint.config.(js|mjs|cjs) file
errorMessages.eslintignoreDeprecated: The .eslintignore file is no longer supported. Switch to using the 'ignores' property in eslint.config.js
errorMessages.migrationSolution: Replace .eslintrc.* and .eslintignore with a flat config file, choosing the right extension / module system for the project
errorMessages.escapeHatchSolution: ONLY on ESLint v9.x: set ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false to keep eslintrc. On v10+ this env var is no longer read and eslintrc is no longer loaded - do NOT suggest this fix without first verifying the installed major is 9.x.

flatConfig.description: Flat ESLint config format - the default for current ESLint releases. Each framework provides both an ESM variant and a CommonJS variant. Choose ESM when the file is eslint.config.mjs OR when eslint.config.js is used with package.json 'type': 'module'. Choose CommonJS when the file is eslint.config.cjs OR when eslint.config.js is used without 'type': 'module' (this is the default Node behavior). Do NOT emit ESM into an eslint.config.js of a CommonJS project - it will throw 'Cannot use import statement outside a module'.

moduleSystemSelection.step: Before emitting a flat config template, read package.json 'type'

legacyConfig.description: Legacy ESLint config format - use only when the installed ESLint version does not support flat config

eslintignore.description: Ignore patterns file - used only with legacy config
eslintignore.note: Not needed for flat config - use the ignores array in eslint.config.js instead

scripts.description: npm scripts to add to package.json for linting. Flat config infers file extensions from the config's files globs; legacy config needs --ext flags.

wrongConfigFormat.problem: ESLint shows error: 'ESLint couldn't find an eslint.config.(js|mjs|cjs) file'
wrongConfigFormat.cause: The installed ESLint no longer auto-searches for eslintrc files and expected a flat config, but only legacy .eslintrc.* files exist

migrate.description: Migrate to flat config (recommended). Create eslint.config.js / .mjs / .cjs, port rules over, then remove the legacy files you've actually replaced.
commands: # Only run after you've ported rules into eslint.config.{js,mjs,cjs}

keepLegacy.description: Keep eslintrc as a migration bridge - ONLY works on ESLint v9.x. Set ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false so ESLint continues to load .eslintrc.* files.
keepLegacy.versionGate: Before recommending this, run 'npx eslint --version' and confirm the major is 9. If it is 10 or higher, this fix does nothing - v10.0.0 (2026-02-06) removed both the env var and eslintrc support. On v10+ migration (option 1) is the only fix.
howTo: Or via environment in CI / dev shell: export ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false
keepLegacy.caveat: Not a long-term solution even on v9.x - the next major already removed it.

wrongConfigFormat.agentRule: Do NOT blindly delete legacy config files. Confirm the project wants to migrate (vs. keep eslintrc via the escape hatch) before running the cleanup command.

eslintignoreDeprecated.problem: Warning: 'The .eslintignore file is no longer supported'
eslintignoreDeprecated.cause: The installed ESLint no longer honors .eslintignore under flat config
eslintignoreDeprecated.solution: Move ignore patterns into the ignores array in the flat config file. Use export default for ESM, module.exports for CommonJS.

parserConflicts.cause: Framework parsers need to be configured in specific order
parserConflicts.solution: Use framework parser as main parser, specify TypeScript parser in parserOptions

importResolution.cause: Import resolver not configured for TypeScript or framework-specific files
importResolution.solution: Configure import resolver in settings section

prettierConflicts.problem: ESLint formatting rules conflict with Prettier
prettierConflicts.cause: ESLint formatting rules enabled alongside Prettier
prettierConflicts.solution: Place eslint-config-prettier LAST in the config chain (last extends entry for legacy, last exported object for flat)

performanceSlow.problem: ESLint is running slowly on large projects
performanceSlow.cause: Linting too many files or complex rules
solutions: Add more ignore patterns (node_modules, dist, coverage)
Disable type-aware rules if not needed (@typescript-eslint/recommended-requiring-type-checking)
Run ESLint only on changed files in pre-commit hooks

esmInCjsProject.problem: SyntaxError: 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' (or similar) when running ESLint with eslint.config.js
esmInCjsProject.cause: eslint.config.js contains ESM (import / export default) but the host package.json does not declare 'type': 'module', so Node loads the file as CommonJS
solutions: Add '"type": "module"' to package.json if the project is meant to be ESM
Rename the file to eslint.config.mjs to force ESM regardless of package.json
Rewrite the file as CommonJS (const x = require(...); module.exports = [...]) and keep eslint.config.js, or rename to eslint.config.cjs
esmInCjsProject.agentRule: Always align the module system of eslint.config.js with package.json 'type' before emitting it. If the project is CommonJS, emit a CommonJS template or use eslint.config.cjs.

testingChecklist: Verify the installed ESLint version is detected correctly (run 'npx eslint --version')
Confirm the correct config format is chosen based on what the installed version supports
Check that the framework is detected correctly from package.json dependencies
Verify TypeScript parser is added if TypeScript is detected (check for typescript in package.json)
Confirm accessibility plugins are included (jsx-a11y for React, vuejs-accessibility for Vue)
Test that ignore patterns work (run lint, verify node_modules/dist/build are ignored)
Run 'npm run lint' to verify configuration works without errors
Run 'npm run lint:fix' to test auto-fix functionality works
Check that import/export organization rules work (imports should be sorted alphabetically)
Verify no-console warnings appear but don't fail the build (warnings should show)
Test that unused variables trigger warnings (create test file with unused variable)
Confirm curly brace enforcement works (if without braces should error)
If Prettier is detected, verify no formatting conflicts exist (no prettier/prettier errors)
Test VS Code integration if ESLint extension is installed (auto-fix on save)
Verify linting works on all file types (.js, .jsx, .ts, .tsx, .vue, .svelte as applicable)
Confirm accessibility rules catch common a11y issues (test img without alt, button without text)
Test that ESLint catches common bugs (== instead of ===, var instead of const/let)
Verify max-depth and complexity warnings appear for deeply nested code
Check that TypeScript-specific rules work if TypeScript is detected (any type should warn)
Test CI/CD integration if applicable (GitHub Actions workflow runs successfully)
